summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration file that sets up a single service called Ollama, which is a containerized application for running large language models. It exposes port 11434, persists data to a volume, and automatically restarts if it crashes. The file uses template variables (marked with %%) that will be replaced with actual values when the compose file is processed.

explanations.6: The container_name uses %%name=ollama%% which is a placeholder syntax that will be replaced with an actual container name when this file is deployed—it's how you can parameterize the configuration.
explanations.8: The port mapping uses %%port=11434%% on the left side, which is another placeholder that will be substituted before deployment, allowing the external port to be customized while the internal port stays 11434.
explanations.10: This mounts a named volume called ollama_data to the path /root/.ollama inside the container, which means any data Ollama writes there will persist even if the container is stopped or deleted.
explanations.11: The restart: always policy tells Docker to automatically restart this container if it ever stops or crashes, ensuring the service stays running.
explanations.21: The volumes section at the top level defines a named volume called ollama_data that Docker will manage for you—it's the storage that gets mounted into the container on line 10.
